blocks.raw: # Customer Name Validation for Loyalty Point Allocation
blocks.text: Customer Name Validation for Loyalty Point Allocation

blocks.raw: ## Requirement
blocks.text: Requirement

blocks.raw: An airline brand needs a validation mechanism to ensure that the first name and last name provided during a flight booking match the customer profile stored on Capillary’s platform. This validation is essential to ensure that loyalty points are allocated to the correct customer.
blocks.text: An airline brand needs a validation mechanism to ensure that the first name and last name provided during a flight booking match the customer profile stored on Capillary’s platform. This validation is essential to ensure that loyalty points are allocated to the correct customer.

blocks.raw: If the provided names do not match either the primary names or any of the stored alternate names (aliases) in the customer profile, the system will not allocate loyalty points.
blocks.text: If the provided names do not match either the primary names or any of the stored alternate names (aliases) in the customer profile, the system will not allocate loyalty points.

blocks.raw: Currently, Capillary’s platform does not offer built-in validation to compare the airline’s booking data with the stored customer records.
blocks.text: Currently, Capillary’s platform does not offer built-in validation to compare the airline’s booking data with the stored customer records.

blocks.raw: ## Solution
blocks.text: Solution

blocks.raw:
To solve this, create [a Neo dataflow](https://eu.intouch.capillarytech.com/extensions/neo/ui/rule/daec5cfa-be66-4d5d-b021-c2f45c3aa322/version/9204edc5-0386-4326-9ef8-9988fe690b64?ruleType=org) that compares the passenger names from the airline record with those stored in the Capillary system.\
**Note**: To view the dataflow, make sure you have access to DocDemo org (100737) and [access to Neo](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/access-management-neo#enabling-neo-extension-access--user-roles).
blocks.text: To solve this, create a Neo dataflow that compares the passenger names from the airline record with those stored in the Capillary system.Note: To view the dataflow, make sure you have access to DocDemo org (100737) and access to Neo.

blocks.raw: ### Step one: Use Schema block to validate input parameters
blocks.text: Step one: Use Schema block to validate input parameters

blocks.raw: Perform schema validation to ensure that all mandatory parameters are present. If any parameter is missing, return an appropriate error response. The required input parameters are:
blocks.text: Perform schema validation to ensure that all mandatory parameters are present. If any parameter is missing, return an appropriate error response. The required input parameters are:

blocks.raw:
* FFN (Frequent Flyer Number)
* First Name (Fname)
* Last Name (lname)
blocks.text: FFN (Frequent Flyer Number)First Name (Fname)Last Name (lname)

blocks.raw: Handle validation failures with the appropriate error messages.
blocks.text: Handle validation failures with the appropriate error messages.

blocks.raw: ### Step two: Use the Script block to create payload for the GET Customer API
blocks.text: Step two: Use the Script block to create payload for the GET Customer API

blocks.raw: Use the Script block to construct valid headers and query parameters, transform data to create a request payload for the GET Customer API call by following these steps:
blocks.text: Use the Script block to construct valid headers and query parameters, transform data to create a request payload for the GET Customer API call by following these steps:

blocks.raw:
* Fetch the input query parameters.
* Remove unnecessary or error-prone headers.
* Build the query using the required values: `externalId`  (FFN) and `source`.
blocks.text: Fetch the input query parameters.Remove unnecessary or error-prone headers.Build the query using the required values: externalId  (FFN) and source.

blocks.raw: ### Step three: Use API Request block to invoke GET Customer API with the appropriate query parameters
blocks.text: Step three: Use API Request block to invoke GET Customer API with the appropriate query parameters

blocks.raw: Use the API Request block to invoke the [https://\{host}/v2/customers/lookup/customerDetails]().
blocks.text: Use the API Request block to invoke the https://{host}/v2/customers/lookup/customerDetails.

blocks.raw: ### Step four: Use the Script block to compare names
blocks.text: Step four: Use the Script block to compare names

blocks.raw: Use the Script block to verify whether the combination of First Name and Last Name from the airline's booking data matches any of the following:
blocks.text: Use the Script block to verify whether the combination of First Name and Last Name from the airline's booking data matches any of the following:

blocks.raw:
* Primary name in the customer profile
* Any of the alternate names (alias1, alias2, alias3)
blocks.text: Primary name in the customer profileAny of the alternate names (alias1, alias2, alias3)

blocks.raw: If there’s a match, return a success response. If not, return a failure response.
blocks.text: If there’s a match, return a success response. If not, return a failure response.
